sections.h2: Does the city of Lexington send its own property tax bill?
sections.html:
No separate city bill exists, because Lexington and Fayette County operate as one government. The Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government (LFUCG) replaced the separate city and county governments in the early 1970s, when police and fire services were merged, and the Fayette County Sheriff collects property tax for the whole territory. The Fayette County PVA, which values every parcel, says on its rate page that the total bill is built from rates set by the Commonwealth, the LFUCG, Fayette County Public Schools and a few other districts.

What differs from one Lexington address to the next is the service district. The PVA's 2026 chart lists seven residential districts that share the same state, school, general services, extension, conservation, health, Lextran and park lines. They diverge only on what the urban government supplies at the curb.

  • The full-service district adds 17.3 cents per $100 for trash pickup, street lights and street cleaning.
  • Districts with only refuse add 13.7 cents, only street lights 2.7 cents, and combinations fall in between.
  • The school line is the biggest piece of every bill at 79.7 cents per $100, about 63 percent of the full-service total of $1.2598.

On a home assessed at $300,000, the gap between the full-service district and the district without optional services is $519 a year. Ask the PVA or the sheriff which district code your parcel carries, since it can change a buyer's monthly cost.

sections.h2: How do blighted-property and downtown charges change a Lexington bill?
sections.html:
Two surcharges apply only in certain places. A property that the LFUCG Vacant Property Review Commission certifies as abandoned and blighted pays an extra $1 per $100 of taxable value. On a $200,000 assessment, that is $2,000 a year on top of the normal bill, which makes a neglected vacant house expensive to hold. A parcel inside the Downtown Lexington Management District pays an extra 10 cents per $100.

If you own a vacant house in Lexington, find out whether it has been certified before listing it. Ask the LFUCG whether your parcel has been certified, and expect any buyer to price the surcharge into an offer.

sections.h2: Why does Lexington's Urban Service Area matter to a seller?
sections.html:
Lexington drew a line around its growth in 1958, the first urban growth boundary in the country. Inside it, the urban service area, builders could develop at city density. Outside it, in the rural service area, the minimum parcel was 40 acres, which protected the horse farms the region is known for. The boundary was widened in 1996 by 5,300 acres, and in 2000 the city adopted a purchase-of-development-rights program that received $40 million in 2001, made of $25 million from local sources and $15 million from the state.

For a seller, the line decides which kind of parcel you have. Property outside it can sit on a large lot in farm use, and Kentucky assesses farmland at agricultural value instead of market value, which changes the tax math completely. Check the tax district and the land use on the PVA's parcel record before you set a price.

The city covers 285.5 square miles, nearly all of it land, and the metropolitan area adds five other counties: Clark, Jessamine, Bourbon, Woodford and Scott. A party of frontiersmen under William McConnell camped at the site in June 1775 and named it for Lexington, Massachusetts, after hearing of the fighting there. Forty-five settlers signed the Lexington Compact on January 25, 1780.

sections.h2: What should I know about Lexington's schools, roads and weather before listing?
sections.html:
Fayette County Public Schools serves the city with six district high schools, 12 middle schools and 37 elementary schools, according to the Lexington entry on Wikipedia, alongside many private schools. The University of Kentucky and Transylvania University are the two traditional colleges, and Blue Grass Airport is on the west side along US 60. I-75 skirts the city and I-64 runs along the north. US 25, 27, 60, 68 and 421 meet in Lexington, which has few freeways and a reputation for congestion.

Weather is moderate and fairly wet. Lexington averages about 49.8 inches of precipitation and 14.5 inches of snow a year, with about 25 days at or above 90 degrees and 23 winter days that never rise above freezing. The Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America also rates the area as high-allergy.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Lexington property tax?
sections.html:
The Fayette County Clerk takes over delinquent bills and has strict payment rules. Because a delinquent bill is a lien, the clerk accepts only cash, money orders or cashier's and certified checks made out to the Fayette County Clerk. Personal checks, business checks and credit cards are refused, and partial payments are not taken. The amount rises every month because of interest. A debtor who cannot pay in full can contact the Fayette County Attorney's Office, at 859-254-4941, about arrangements.

The clerk's office is at 162 E. Main Street, Room 132, Lexington, KY 40507, and answers payoff questions at 859-253-3344 from 8:00 to 4:30. A search tool and calculator are on the clerk's deeds website. Each year the clerk sells eligible delinquent bills to third-party purchasers, at a date between 90 and 135 days after the sheriff hands the list over. The 2026 sale took place on July 24 at 11:00 a.m., and instructions for the 2027 sale are scheduled for spring 2027. For a seller, the lesson is simple: get the payoff before the listing goes live.

sections.h2: What do Lexington sellers owe when the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Kentucky's transfer tax under KRS 142.050 is 50 cents for every $500 of the stated price, rounded up for any fraction, and the grantor owes it. On a $325,000 sale that comes to $325. The county clerk figures the amount and collects it before accepting the deed, and it is paid once per transaction in the county where the deed must be recorded. Foreclosure transfers, transfers between spouses in a divorce, and parent-to-child transfers for nominal consideration are exempt.

Property tax follows its own track. The bill goes to whoever held title on January 1, and the contract or settlement statement decides how the year is split. Homeowners 65 or older, or totally disabled, may already have the $49,100 homestead exemption for 2025 and 2026, and a buyer has to apply again with the Fayette County PVA.

faqs.q: Is there a separate city property tax in Lexington?
faqs.a: No. Lexington and Fayette County share one urban county government, so the single bill from the Fayette County Sheriff covers state, school, county and urban-government charges. Rates depend on the service district of your address.

faqs.q: What is the biggest part of a Lexington tax bill?
faqs.a: The school line. The PVA's 2026 chart sets it at 79.7 cents per $100 of assessed value in every residential district, against a full-service total of $1.2598.

faqs.q: How much extra does a blighted Lexington property pay?
faqs.a: An extra $1 per $100 of taxable value once the LFUCG Vacant Property Review Commission certifies it as abandoned and blighted. On a $200,000 assessment that is $2,000 a year.

faqs.q: Can I pay delinquent Lexington tax with a credit card?
faqs.a: No. The Fayette County Clerk takes only cash, money orders and cashier's or certified checks for delinquent bills, and it does not accept partial payments.

faqs.q: What is the Lexington transfer tax on a home sale?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents per $500 of value under KRS 142.050, charged to the seller and collected by the county clerk at recording. A $325,000 sale produces $325.
